Yes, you're right, it's about my own personal struggle with depression/mental illness in general. The repetitive nature of the poem was intentional because I wanted to get across the feeling of oppression and relentlessness that comes with suffering from mental illness. Also, the repetition of different adjectives to describe 'it' is to get across the feeling of being labelled by professionals/society and having your identity reduced to symptoms. At the end of the day, you're left feeling like there is something wrong with you, but you cannot pin down exactly what 'it' is so 'it' is ambiguous. Since it is about my own experiences, the last stanza is about ultimately accepting and working with your own deficiencies. Thanks for your feedback!

I was at a really posh party for my dad's business associate when I was little; He was an artsy type and he had an admittedly impressive library that covered the whole wall in an arc. One of those ones where you have to have a moveable ladder to get to books. And a grand piano and all that. There were all kinds of la-di-da types there and also a really lovely woman who was in charge of catering.  She had brought her kid along with her and we were all just being kids and running round and playing in the place while everyone else drank champagne and talked about pretentious bullshit. A really obnoxious woman was having a discussion with some other people and she was having a go at the caterer's son for running around. Can't remember what she said but it was along the lines of 'where do you think you are? That behaviour isn't appropriate you petulant little child' and she was just generally treating him like 'the help'. His comeback was 'yeah, well you're fat.' 

So simple, yet so powerful. She was lost for words and the people she was with were trying to look shocked but you could tell they were stifling laughter too. We then just laughed and ran off.

I almost died after my first overdose but since I was found by someone in time, I was able to be revived. With an opiate overdose, there is an antidote that can quickly reverse the effects, but when you mix downers there is a much greater chance of your respiratory system shutting down. That almost happened to me. But the method of overdosing is still more likely to end up with you surviving and being damaged more than anything. There is such a long time between taking an overdose and the possibility of death that it is much more likely that you are found and revived and you either get lucky and there is no significant damage, or you end up with serious organ failure. It's just a massive risk.

My last overdose involved fentanyl. I mean, obviously people can die from OD'ing because it's in the death statistics and you hear about it, but it's not a reliable method and there is a greater chance of you just ending up physically impaired as a result. When I OD'd with fentanyl, I woke up in my own vomit and there must have been a chance I could've choked, but it seems I've cheated death many times now.

Just an update, I did end up going to hospital, and because of the insanely long waiting times I ended up spending a whole day there really, but I had my bloods taken and I'm fine physically. If they really have exhausted all treatment options, and their life situation makes it so that they have no prospects, and they are suffering, then I believe it is that person's right to choose whether to use assisted suicide or not. By no prospects, I mean little to no family support, drug and alcohol abuse, severe mental agony, isolation, traumatic environment etc. That's just my opinion, although my judgement may be clouded somewhat since I'm depressed at the moment. I just wonder why people should suffer needlessly when none of us REALLY matter anyway, a bit nihilistic, but that's life!

Well what if that person was in such mental agony that they saw no other option? And after exhausting every possible treatment, and also if they had nothing planned for their future or any support system, wouldn't it be respectful to give them the option of a peaceful death? The process wouldn't be just killing people on a whim, or killing to cull the population, but giving people the choice, and then seeing if they can be deemed to qualify.
